Identify cell-type niches from NMF latent factors

compute_cells_niches.Rd

For each NMF factor, extracts the top-contributing cell group parts (<group>_pos / <group>_neg, by basis weight, see extract_contributing_features()), maps them to their constituent cell types (compute.composition.matrix()), and keeps only cell types enriched relative to the background composition. Saves a star-network PDF per factor and returns the weighted cell-type associations.

Usage

compute_cells_niches(
  latent_factors,
  dt,
  cell.groups,
  enrich_thresh = 1.5,
  quantile_cutoff = 0.7,
  cells_extra = NULL,
  return = TRUE,
  file_name = NULL
)

Arguments

latent_factors

A list returned by compute.latent_factors(), containing W (features x factors) and the NMF model object.

dt

A named list of deconvolution subgroup results, used to build the cell-group composition matrix via compute.composition.matrix().

cell.groups

A list of cell group definitions as returned by construct_cell_groups().

enrich_thresh

Numeric. Minimum enrichment ratio (see above) for a cell type to be retained per factor. Default 1.5.

quantile_cutoff

Numeric between 0 and 1. Quantile threshold for selecting top-contributing cell group parts per factor (see extract_contributing_features()). Default 0.7.

cells_extra

Optional character vector of additional cell type names, added to the vocabulary used to recognise cell types in the feature names (see compute.composition.matrix()).

return

Logical. If TRUE, saves network PDF plots to Results/Network_<factor>_<file_name>.pdf (Results/Network_<factor>.pdf without file_name). Default TRUE.

file_name

Character. Suffix appended to output file names.

Value

A named list (one element per factor with at least one enriched cell type) of named numeric vectors giving the enriched cell types and their weights, sorted descending.

Details

For each factor and cell type:

  • the weight is the sum of the NMF weights of the selected parts whose cell group contains the cell type;

  • the enrichment is the fraction of selected parts containing the cell type divided by the fraction of all cell groups containing it. It is a ratio, not a statistical test: with few selected parts, a cell type present in only one of them can pass the threshold.

The direction is not taken into account: a selected part can mean more or fewer cells of its group (depending on _pos / _neg and on whether the features of the group are positively or negatively related to its TF module), and both are added together. A cell type of a niche is therefore associated with the factor, without saying whether the factor has more or fewer of it.

Examples

data("network.tuto")
data("deconv_subgroups.tuto")
cell_groups <- construct_cell_groups(network.tuto, deconv_subgroups.tuto)
#> 20 of 764 features were not assigned to any cluster by the tree cut and are not part of any cell group (blue: 6, pink: 2, red: 2, yellow: 8, black: 2)
latent <- compute.latent_factors(cell_groups$Cell_groups, return = FALSE)
#> Estimating optimal rank via elbow on reconstruction MSE (ranks 2:8)...
#> MSE by rank: k2=0.00127  k3=0.000964  k4=0.000838  k5=0.000756  k6=0.00071  k7=0.000675  k8=0.000632
#> Selected rank (elbow): 3
#> Running RcppML NMF with rank = 3...
niches <- compute_cells_niches(latent, deconv_subgroups.tuto, cell_groups, return = FALSE)
niches
#> $Factor1
#>                  CAF               Plasma           NK.resting 
#>           0.14005451           0.08621658           0.07939530 
#> Mast.activated.cells          Eosinophils 
#>           0.04995649           0.03483520 
#> 
#> $Factor2
#> Mast.activated.cells 
#>           0.05231772 
#> 
#> $Factor3
#>             B.cells T.cells.gamma.delta 
#>          0.35303595          0.02312485
